newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Labour increases large poll lead.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Labour increases large poll lead.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party increased its lead over the ruling Conservatives after leader Tony Blair gave a rousing speech to the party's pre-election annual conference, the Sunday Times newspaper said.
The NOP poll said Labour's rating rose to 52 percent after Tuesday's speech from 50 percent while the percentage of people supporting the Conservatives fell to 29 percent from 31 percent.
The minority Liberal Democrats fell to 13 percent from 14 percent in the poll, which NOP carried out on Thursday by interviewing 1,543 electors.

A Gallup survey in Saturday's Daily Telegraph said Labour's rating had risen to 57 percent after the speech from 52 percent before it, while the percentage of people supporting the ruling Conservatives fell to 24 from 27.5.
Gallup interviewed 1,047 electors between September 26 and October 1 for its initial survey, and then questioned 587 people on October 3 and 4 to test the effect of Blair's speech.
Prime Minister John Major, who will address the annual Conservative conference next Friday, must call an election by May next year.
